title: Graphing an Upward-Shifted Inverse-Square Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1/x^2 + 1 by identifying its parent function, shift, asymptotes, domain, range, and intercepts.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \frac{1}{x^2} \text{ shifted up } 1;\quad \text{VA: } x = 0,\quad \text{HA: } y = 1,\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, 0) \cup (0, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (1, \infty),\quad \text{Intercepts: none}

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Vertical Shift
steps.explanation: Adding 1 to the parent function y = 1/x^2 shifts its graph 1 unit upward.
steps.why: Adding 1 increases every output of 1/x^2 by 1.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote is x = 0, and the horizontal asymptote shifts up to y = 1. Because 1/x^2 > 0 for all x != 0, 1/x^2 + 1 > 1, giving range (1, infinity).
steps.why: Shifting the range (0, infinity) upward by 1 yields (1, infinity).

steps.title: Verify Intercepts and Symmetry
steps.explanation: Because x != 0 and y > 1 everywhere, the graph never intersects either coordinate axis. Both branches lie above y = 1, symmetric about the y-axis and passing through (+/-1, 2).
steps.why: Since 1/x^2 + 1 >= 1 > 0, y can never equal 0, and x = 0 is excluded from the domain.
